title: Add per-metric click-to-chart for Air Quality columns
description:
Main-page Air Quality columns (Humidity, CO2, VOC, Radon, PM2.5, PM1) should behave like Temperature and Illuminance: clicking a cell opens a time-series chart for that metric, with the clicked device pre-selected and all other devices available as checkboxes.

Data: all six metrics are already logged to devlog.status_json every minute via update_from_airthings; full per-device history exists.

Approach: single parameterized /metric_chart?metric=<name>&device_ids=<id> page + /api/v1/metric?metric=<name> endpoint, mirroring the illuminance chart pattern. Cell links only rendered when that device actually has data for that metric (same pattern as has_illuminance).

Out of scope (follow-on): CSV download on metric and lighting chart pages.
notes:
Design decisions:
- One parameterized page + one parameterized API endpoint, not six copies. Config table maps URL metric name -> {status_json key, display label, unit, y-axis formatter, decimals}. Note radon's URL name 'radon' maps to status_json key 'radonShortTermAvg'.
- New db helper get_device_metric_series(conn, status_key, value_path, device_ids) generalizes get_lighting_series. Values are nested as status_json[key].value (Airthings structure); helper must unwrap.
- Per-device/per-metric gating: get_device_status extended to set has_humidity/has_co2/has_voc/has_radon/has_pm25/has_pm1 booleans, mirroring has_illuminance logic. Template only renders chart link when the flag is set.
- Radon chart must respect user's existing Bq/m3 <-> pCi/L unit preference (currently honored in unit_speed.js).
- CSV download deferred to hvac-yhq; will be added to both this new page and the lighting chart at the same time.
Implementation complete and verified via curl + unit tests. All 6 metric pages render (200), invalid metric rejected (400), API returns per-device series correctly filtered by device_ids. Cell gating verified: Airthings devices expose all 6 metric links, Hubitat sensors expose only humidity (matches their data). Radon tooltip precision fixed per advisor: 1 decimal in pCi/L mode, 0 in Bq/m³.

Awaiting browser verification from user (CLI environment can't launch browser):
- Click CO2 cell -> chart renders with clicked device pre-selected
- Click Hubitat humidity cell (e.g. device 15) -> cross-source data renders
- Radon chart + C/F toggle -> y-axis, tooltip unit, and values all rescale
- Temporal picker (day/week/month/all) -> reloads data

Tests added (all passing):
- test_get_device_metric_series_airthings_dict
- test_get_device_metric_series_hubitat_scalar
- test_get_device_metric_series_skips_missing
- test_get_device_status_sets_aq_metric_flags
- test_metric_endpoint_accepts_known_metrics
- test_metric_endpoint_rejects_unknown_metric
- test_metric_chart_page_renders
Browser-verified by user on 2026-04-21. Caught missing #metric-chart height CSS rule (chart div needs explicit height for echarts; ported 620px rule from #lighting-chart into style.css).
close_reason: Shipped. Per-metric click-to-chart for Humidity/CO2/VOC/Radon/PM2.5/PM1 on home page, browser-verified.

title: Rooms should not have Back buttons
description:
The rooms pages (Hickory and Kitchen) have a back button in the top left ("-> Main").
This is useful when the page is invoked from the app main menu.

But these pages are also intended to be used on standalone tables, where this escape
should not be offered.

So, make this conditional. The invocation from the app should add and `embedded` flag
parameter to the URL.

title: Enhance hickory page
description:
This issue includes several tasks.

Implement each one separately, and pause for the user to test each, before committing
and continuing to the next task. All of the tasks in this issue refer to the Hickory
room page.

Note that some backend support for this was added in recent commits 2370b69 and
a5e8e19. You will need to understand this code. You may also need to add additional
similar code to support some of these new features.

Note also that our work today replaces features that are already supported by a Hubitat
dashboard page:
http://10.2.3.51/apps/api/538/dashboard/538?access_token=a161dd5b-8f38-4323-8f2c-2f2ed330bb0e
You may find it useful to examine that page, since it my have some useful insights for
our implementation too.

Here are the tasks:

# Task 1: Add the "Hickory Sensor" temperature and humidity to this page.

# Task 2: Add the current date and time (just down to minutes; no seconds) to this
  page. It should update without the user needing to manually refresh.

# Task 3: Remove A51-n sensors display. Remove the Temperature Sensors section of this
  page that shows sensors A51-1 through A51-4 and A51 Hallway.

# Task 4: Control TV Position. The Hickory Room has a TV that can be moved to the Up or
  Down position.  Add UI to this page to show the current position and allow the user to
  change it.

# Task 5: Light dimmer. The room has dimmable lights.  Add the ability to see the
  current level and adjust it using a tasteful slider or dial.

# Task 6: Other lights. There should also be on/off controls for the inner green wall
  lights and outer green wall lights.
close_reason: All 6 tasks complete: Hickory Sensor with humidity, live clock, A51 sensor removal with offline handling, TV control, light dimmer, wall light toggles. Plus layout compaction and Room Controls tile grid redesign.

title: Home page: show time until rules re-enable
description: On the home page, add a new column that, when rules have been disabled for a device, shows the remaining hours:minutes until the rule will automatically re-enable.
notes:
Design decisions (2026-04-20):
- Label: 'Resume'
- Placement: right after Unit column, rowspan=2 in ERV/FCU tables only (Air Quality skipped — no rules applied there)
- Format: H:MM (e.g. '2:15', '0:30'); dash '—' when rules are active
- Effective timer = max(per-device disabled_until, master rules_engine disabled_until). Option A.
- Impl: add 'rules_master_disabled_until' as top-level key in /api/v1/status response (since rules_engine pseudo-device has no devlog row and is excluded from get_device_status). Compute effective client-side.
- Refresh reuses existing 1-sec refreshGridRows tick.
- Existing 'rules disabled' superscript kept for now (user: 'mostly for debugging, will remove soon').
2026-04-20 (round 2):
- Column renamed 'Resume Rules' → 'Disable for' (matches common UX phrasing better than 'Disabled Until' since the displayed value is remaining duration).
- Added −/+ adjustment buttons in each row's cell, styled like settemp thermostat widget.
- Semantics: +/- modify per-device disabled_until (not the global timer); hidden when rules active (dash). + snaps up to next 30-min boundary, − snaps down; if result <= now it clamps to 0 (re-enables).
- New endpoint: POST /api/v1/set_device_disabled_until body {device_id, disabled_until}; past timestamp clamps to 0.
- Dropped all_rules_disabled_until from /status since per-device is now authoritative for this column.
2026-04-20 (round 2 — correction):
Rounding is applied to *remaining minutes* (duration), not wall-clock time. The click reads the currently displayed minute count (ceil seconds/60), and snaps UP for + or DOWN for − to the nearest multiple of 30. This is drift-free: e.g. clicking + when '1:00' is displayed always yields 90 min, regardless of sub-minute jitter from the 1-sec refresh.
2026-04-20 (final):
- Optimistic UI: button clicks update the cell immediately and debounce the server POST by 400ms so rapid clicks coalesce. Refresh loop skips server updates for a device while its write is pending; a sequence number disambiguates late-resolving older POSTs.
- Cell centering: column text-align changed to center so rows with/without buttons line up vertically.
- Renamed HTML IDs and CSS classes from 'resume' to 'disable-for' for consistency with the final column label.

title: Migrate beads from server mode to embedded mode
description: This project was initialized when beads v0.55-0.56 only supported server mode. As of v0.63.3/v1.0.0, embedded mode is the default and simpler (no dolt-server process to manage). Migration path: bd backup init, bd backup sync, bd init (re-initialize as embedded), bd backup restore --force.

title: Use per-device API calls in hickory_room_status
description:
hickory_room_status (routes_api.py) currently calls hubitat.get_all_devices() and filters by ID to read attributes like level and switch. Some Hubitat Maker API firmware versions don't return full attributes on the all-devices endpoint, which would cause the dimmer to always show 0% and lights to show off.

Switch to calling hubitat.get_device_info(device_id) for each configured device (dimmer_id, wall_inner_id, wall_outer_id). This trades 1 HTTP call for 3, but guarantees full attribute data.

This also resolves the dead-code issue: get_device_info() in hubitat.py was added in the hickory-room branch but has no callers yet.
notes:
Implementation plan:
1. In hickory_room_status(), replace the get_all_devices() + by_id lookup with individual get_device_info() calls for each configured device ID
2. Wrap each call in its own try/except so one device being unreachable doesn't break the whole response
3. Update test_room_status_returns_device_states to mock hubitat.get_device_info instead of get_all_devices
4. Update test_room_status_missing_devices — get_device_info will raise or return empty for missing devices
5. Verify against the actual Hubitat hub that attributes (level, switch) are present in the single-device response

title: Generalize hardcoded /hickory/ API routes for any room
description:
The four Hickory room control endpoints (room_status, dimmer, wall_light, tv) are hardcoded under /api/v1/hickory/ and look up room_config.ROOM_CONFIGS.get('hickory', {}). If another room (e.g. kitchen) ever needs similar controls, these routes would need to be duplicated.

Refactor to accept the room name as a URL parameter (e.g. /api/v1/room/<location>/dimmer) and look up the config dynamically, similar to how routes_web.py already handles /kitchen and /hickory with a shared _render_room_dashboard_with_data().
notes: Only worth doing when a second room actually needs controls. Not a bug — just coupling to watch for.
